findings.title: OAuth redirect URL is built by string concatenation without URL-encoding parameters
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the GitHub authorize redirect is constructed as f"{ghip.get_oauth_authorize_url()}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}". None of the query parameters are URL-encoded. The redirect_uri (built from absolute_uri(reverse(...))) and the state (pipeline.signature) are interpolated raw. If any of these values contain characters like '&', '=', '#', or spaces, the resulting URL will be malformed or the parameters will be split/overridden, which can break the OAuth flow or, in a crafted scenario, allow parameter injection into the authorize URL. The correct approach is to use urllib.parse.urlencode to build the query string.

findings.title: safe_urlopen to GitHub token endpoint is not wrapped in try/except; network/HTTP errors will raise unhandled exceptions
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data) at line 423 without any exception handling. The subsequent try/except only wraps safe_urlread(req) and parse_qsl, not the urlopen call itself. If GitHub's token endpoint returns a non-2xx status (safe_urlopen raises on HTTP errors) or the network request fails/times out, an unhandled exception propagates out of the pipeline view, producing a 500 error instead of the intended user-facing error page. The PR description explicitly claims the pipeline fails gracefully when 'GitHub could not generate correct access_token from the code', but a non-200 response from the token endpoint will not be handled gracefully.

findings.body: After obtaining the access_token, OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) at line 434 with no exception handling. get_user_info makes an HTTP request to GitHub's /user endpoint; if that request fails (network error, rate limit, 401/403 from GitHub, non-JSON response), an exception propagates and the user gets a 500 error rather than the friendly 'Invalid installation request' error page. The code only checks whether 'login' is present in the returned dict, but does not handle the case where the call itself raises.

findings.title: User-mismatch check crashes with KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the check pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] accesses integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] directly. However, 'sender' is only set in build_integration when state.get("sender") is truthy (line 376-377), and it is entirely possible for an Integration created via the GitHub webhook (installation event) to have metadata without a 'sender' key, or with a sender dict lacking 'login'. In that case this line raises KeyError (or TypeError if metadata['sender'] is not a dict), producing an unhandled 500 error during the installation flow instead of either proceeding or showing the error page. The check should use .get() with a safe default, e.g. integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login").

findings.body: The state parameter validation at line 412 uses a plain string comparison: if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature. For OAuth/OIDC state parameters, which are security tokens meant to prevent CSRF, the comparison should be performed in constant time (e.g. usinghmac.compare_digest or secrets.compare_digest) to avoid timing attacks that could theoretically allow an attacker to recover the expected state value byte-by-byte. While the practical exploitability here is limited (the state is a pipeline signature tied to a server-side session), using a non-constant-time comparison for a security token is a recognized weakness and the standard library provides compare_digest precisely for this purpose.
